short: Direct Bandgap Light Emission from Strained Germanium Nanowi
title: Direct Bandgap Light Emission from Strained Germanium Nanowires Coupled with High-Q Nanophotonic Cavities

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Silicon photonics needs an efficient CMOS-compatible on-chip light source; indirect-gap Ge emits weakly. High tensile strain in a Ge nanowire inside a high-Q cavity should narrow the direct gap and give strong direct-gap emission and gain.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/architecture), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Uniform ~2.4% uniaxial tensile strain along the narrow central nanowire, falling off through the tapers, as the FEM design predicts. Fabricated device reproduces the designed geometry: narrow nanowire joining two rounded pads, flanked by curved multi-line DBR mirrors

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Direct-gap emission red-shifts from ~1560 nm to beyond ~1980 nm with strain, i.e. the direct gap narrows.
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (PRP/value), n13 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n17 (PRP/value), n18 (PRP/value), n19 (MEC/tradeoff). Premises: Tensile strain reduces the Ge bandgap; Free carriers lower the refractive index and add absorption: cavity modes blue-shift and broaden with carrier density

states.title: Performance state
states.head: No lasing: resonances broaden rather than narrow up to 45 mW pulsed pumping, despite high strain and ~1e19 doping

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Strained Ge nanowires in high-Q DBR cavities give strongly enhanced, red-shifted direct-gap emission with Q~2000 modes, but valence-band free-carrier absorption keeps net gain negative, so no lasing

nodes.note: 2.37% maximum not resolved separately from 1.95%; text gives ~1560 -> >=1980 nm

nodes.title: PL, F4
nodes.head: Peak PL intensity ~250 (0%) vs ~1100 envelope with resonances up to ~2700 (1.95%) and ~1100 (2.37%). 2.37% envelope is no brighter than 1.95% and rolls off inside the grey detection-limit band above 2000 nm
nodes.solves: Direct-gap PL intensity rises strongly in strained nanowires compared with the unstrained wire
nodes.note: strong rise from 0% to strained; resonance fringes visible on 1.95% trace, weaker on 2.37%; ~12 nm spacing of adjacent resonances text attributes the apparent short-wavelength peak of the 2.37% wire to the InGaAs detector cutoff

nodes.title: evidence, F4, F5
nodes.head: All resonances shift ~4-6 nm to shorter wavelength and broaden as pump power rises from ~5 to 45 mW. Measured net gain vs carrier density follows the model above ~5e19 cm-3 but lies ~150-250 cm-1 below it at 2-4e19 cm-3
nodes.solves: Free-carrier absorption grows faster with injection than the strain-enhanced direct-gap gain, so net gain drops with pumping
nodes.op: compare across conditions, overlay model on data
nodes.note: each row normalised; OCR annotations 'orm','ntensit' are fragments of the colour-bar label model is EPM per caption; OCR reads panel letter as (q)
nodes.detail: o14: All resonances shift ~4-6 nm to shorter wavelength and broaden as pump power rises from ~5 to 45 mW; o17: Measured net gain vs carrier density follows the model above ~5e19 cm-3 but lies ~150-250 cm-1 below it at 2-4e19 cm-3
nodes.necessity_reason: n19 keeps shown support from o19 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Net gain negative at all powers, falling from ~-350/-500 cm-1 at 5 mW to ~-1250/-2000 cm-1 at 22.5 mW
nodes.solves: Net optical gain stays negative and falls further as pump power (carrier density) increases
nodes.note: CW 980 nm pump per caption; gain-extraction method in SI (not in packet)
nodes.detail: o15: Net gain negative at all powers, falling from ~-350/-500 cm-1 at 5 mW to ~-1250/-2000 cm-1 at 22.5 mW
